gaps.criterion_why: A player watching a grass fire would see whether it runs downwind rather than just being blocked sideways, so asking the scene to tell wind-following apart from a wind-blind lane block, with a reversed-wind case and a clean start, is a fair bar that a correct mod can pass.
gaps.judge_criterion_why: His bar is that the fire walks with the wind. A scene that never varies the wind cannot show the wind is the cause, and the contract requires a control that rules out the plausible alternative.
gaps.observed: The leaf asks that the player 'sees it run with the wind, away from where it lit, and not spread evenly to every side', and that it 'must not read as a fire that spreads the same way whatever the wind'. Its red is 'a line burns as far upwind as downwind'. The scene's action lights 'a short line at the upwind end of each strip', so the strip holds no upwind grass to read. Its only varied input is the setting: one wind, 'the wind set across them' (the script calls SetWindForTest "90" once, east). The script lights the line at x+2. Its row 'the burn moves downwind' (east_cells >= 4) is never compared with the off control, whose expect reads only 'the burn spreads into the outer lanes on both sides'. The one discriminating read is 'nothing burns in the lanes beside it', and a build that suppresses lateral spread whatever the wind (or spreads along one axis only) passes it. The rules_out, 'an instrument blind to vanilla's even spread passing an unmoved fire as walking', shows the instrument can see, not that the wind is the mechanism. The start's wind is not asserted: the script records wind_set and ProbeWind but never checks them. The strips being fire-free before lighting is not read. exam.json e1, e2 and c1 judge this leaf on whether the upwind ground stays unburned, which the scene cannot read.

gaps.would_pass: sc_fire_walks_with_wind lights the line with grass on both sides of it along the wind axis, at least as many cells upwind as downwind are planted. It asserts that the downwind reach exceeds the upwind reach with the wind on, and that the off control's upwind and downwind reach are about equal. A second case with the wind reversed (or turned 90 degrees) on the same layout asserts that the burn's long axis follows the new wind. The start asserts that ProbeWind reads the set direction and that each strip's fire count is 0 before lighting. A script or fresh judge can check each of these rows in the scene's output.
